newsitem.title: UK: Guinness/GrandMet say no row with LVMH over merger.
newsitem.headline: Guinness/GrandMet say no row with LVMH over merger.

text.p: Grand Metropolitan and Guinness said on Monday there had been no row with Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods and drinks group LVMH Moet Hennessy and a non-executive director of Guinness, who has voted against their proposed merger.

"Let me assure you that there has not been any sort of row between ourselves and LVMH. We have had a number of very commercial, professional and sensible discussions about this," Tony Greener, joint chairman of the merged group said.
"There's no doubt that there is an alternative solution that Bernard Arnault would prefer," Greener told a press briefing.

He denied that the relationship with LVMH, which has a 14.2-percent shareholding in Guinness, was effectively dead. "Absolutely not. We have a lot of mutual interests and benefits from our joint venture," Greener said.

There was no acrimony between the two and workmanlike discussions would carry on over the coming weeks. Greener said Arnault had been told of the plans at the same time as other Guinness board members about two weeks ago.
Asked if Arnault would be offered a place on the board of the merged company, to be called GMG Brands, Greener said "That's not for me to say".

When told of the plan, Arnault wrote to the heads of the British groups to propose combining the three spirits and wines businesses of GrandMet, Guinness and Moet Hennessy as an independent listed group.
